text:
marta: hitting weird mem growth on a long-context Mistral run. after ~20k tokens the host shows +15% GPU mem and the KV map size jumps. looks like pages are being duplicated instead of moved. anyone seen "stitch migration" before?

raj: hmm, "stitch migration"? can you paste the trace? is this on MQA or GQA variant?

marta: repro is on mistral-7b-gqa, rope scaling enabled. repro harness attached below. here's the relevant log window: 
```
[2026-02-18T14:01:12Z] kv_assign: slot=0x3a2 anchor=0x1f2 len=8192 -> page 122
[2026-02-18T14:01:12Z] kv_stitch: migrating pages 122 -> 204 (overlap=0x40)
[2026-02-18T14:01:12Z] kv_clone: page 122 refcnt++ (now 2)
[2026-02-18T14:01:13Z] kv_evict: candidate=122 skipped (stale-kv-shadow)
[2026-02-18T14:01:14Z] kv_map_size: 12.4MB -> 14.2MB (unexpected)
```

marta: note the clone refcnt bump — we end up with two identical pages mapped for different anchors. that's the growth.

sasha: do we do copy-on-write during stitch? should be a move not a clone unless there's a concurrent reader. maybe a race with batching. what batching mode were you using?

marta: continuous-batch heuristic on (latency-first), batch horizon=12. I see high concurrency on short completion fragments.

ben: this smells like slot-affinity + anchor drift. rope scaling moves the anchor and we try to stitch into an occupied slot; kernel falls back to clone to avoid breaking in-flight KV reads. clone never gets GC'd because eviction checks use a stale signature.

ana: @marta can you run the repro with KV_DEBUG=stitch and attach the perf counters? I want the eviction/pass stats.

marta: ran with KV_DEBUG=stitch, KV_EVICT=1. counters: 
```
stitch_attempts: 83
stitch_clones: 45
evict_skipped_due_to_shadow: 41
evict_success: 2
per_token_alloc: +0.27kb
```

marta: eviction skipped ratio ~98% of attempts. that explains net growth.

raj: interesting. kernel selection might be doing a safe-path clone on our general-purpose kernel. we should add a specialized "stitch-move" kernel when rope scaling is active — it can grab anchors with a brief lock and avoid clone. downside is slightly higher latency on the critical path.

ben: agree. alternative: change batching heuristic to reduce concurrent reads that cross anchor boundaries. e.g., prefer smaller batch horizon for rope-enabled models OR bias kernel to prefer in-place move if refcnt==1.

sasha: both approaches valid. I worry about races: if a concurrent read shows refcnt==1 then increments to 2 before move. need atomic compare-and-swap of mapping pointer. kernel-level CAS is best.

infra-bot: @marta created perf trace: https://internal.redwood/trace/2177654321/kv-stitch-mistral.zip (expires in 7d)

marta: thanks. I ran an experiment: toggled batch_horizon 12->4, and stitch_clones dropped 45->6, evict_skipped 41->3, mem growth flattened. throughput drops 7% on our harness.

ana: good signal. can we try a kernel patch that performs atomic-page-swap (fast path) and falls back to clone only if contention? if that works, perf hit should be <2%.

raj: i'll prototype atomic-page-swap in the kernel. will emulate using an atomic pointer swap to page table entry, plus a GC fence. If we can guarantee readers always see consistent page numbers, we can avoid the clone.

ben: also add a telemetry tag when stitch_clone happens: model, rope_scale, batch_horizon, kernel_version. we need to correlate in prod.

marta: created a quick perf note in testcase: 
```
# repro harness snippet
python run_long_context.py --model mistral-7b-gqa --rope-scale 1.5 --tokens 25000 --batching continuous --horizon 12
```

marta: next steps: raj -> kernel prototype (atomic swap), sasha -> add batch heuristic toggle, ben -> telemetry tags, ana -> schedule canary on dedicated with small traffic. i'll run longer overnight reproductions.

sasha: also add unit that simulates reader contended window; we should test race window explicitly.

raj: starting kernel PR today, will post diff. expect initial microbenchmark by EOD.

marta: great. thanks all :thumbsup:

ben: fyi, this might also show up for qwen when rope-anchor drift is non-linear (we saw similar but quieter behavior last month). keep an eye.

marta: noted. i'll add qwen+mistral matrix to test plan.

ana: ping if you want me to run the canary schedule.

marta: will do. end of thread.
